characterization_methods.key_findings: YS virtually unchanged by aging; UTS and TE reduced
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, averages of three measurements

characterization_methods.key_findings: hardness slightly increased by aging; ~200 HBW (Fig. 3d)
fully recrystallized microstructure with grain size ~20 μm and retained Mn microsegregations
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Aging (550 °C, 24 h) leaves YS virtually unchanged and slightly increases hardness, but reduces UTS and TE; embrittlement is most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; a 4-kg ingot was successively filled with melt.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 10×50×130 mm³ blocks → 2±0.1 mm thick, ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sheets were reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, then cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into segments (2×60×55 mm³).
Aging was conducted in air at 550 °C for 24 h, followed by oil quenching; this is the specific aging condition for this sample.
Scales were removed from surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile testing with initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; all plotted values are averages of three measurements for every material state; hardness reported in HBW.

elongation.value: reduced relative to as-homogenized state (77% TE)

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: reduced relative to as-homogenized state (830 MPa)

yield_strength.value: virtually unchanged from as-homogenized state (360 MPa); Fig. 3a shows ~350–450 MPa at 0Al

unmapped_findings: For the Al-free reference material (Fe-30Mn-1.2C), the best mechanical behavior is the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE); aging leaves YS virtually unchanged and slightly increases hardness, but reduces UTS and TE, with embrittlement most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C). This 550 °C/24 h sample falls in the embrittled long-aging, high-temperature regime.

This sample is the Al-free (0 wt.% Al) reference of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl SIMPLEX TWIP set; no κ-carbide precipitation is reported for the Al-free alloy, so the observed aging-induced UTS/TE reduction is not attributed to κ-carbides in the text.

The paper presents a temperature-sensitive constitutive strain-hardening model for single-phase low-density TWIP (SIMPLEX) steels (three dislocation densities plus twin volume fraction), applicable in principle to this Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample; however, no simulation results are reported specifically for this sample (model validation in Fig. 7 uses a Fe-22wt.%Mn-0.6wt.%C model TWIP steel).
